name: Metroplex
ownershipStory: Atkins founded Metroplex in 1985 to release his own Model 500 material after major labels showed no interest in Detroit's machine music. Unlike Trax in Chicago, Metroplex stayed artist-owned from the start, a structure Derrick May's Transmat and Kevin Saunderson's KMS both followed.
hook: Detroit's first artist-owned techno label, started because nobody else would put the records out.

blurb.age7: Juan Atkins started his own record label, Metroplex, so he could release his own machine music.
blurb.age13: Atkins founded Metroplex in 1985 after struggling to interest existing labels in Detroit's new electronic sound. Releasing his own music as Model 500, he set a pattern other Detroit techno artists followed: keep the label, and the masters, in the artist's own hands.
blurb.adult: Metroplex is the founding document of Detroit techno as a self-published genre. Its artist-ownership model, unusual for dance music at the time, is one reason Detroit techno artists mostly avoided the rights disputes that plagued Chicago house labels like Trax.
